name: Daihatsu
overview: Pioneers of compact 3-cylinder economy cars and nimble mini-4x4s, beloved for the Charade, Rocky, and Feroza.
australian_history:
Daihatsu arrived in Australia in 1967 with the Compagno 800 and 1000 range of sedans, wagons, and utilities. In 1977, Daihatsu launched the G10 Charade, powered by an innovative 993cc 3-cylinder engine. The Charade was hailed for its exceptional packaging and fuel efficiency, winning the 1979 Wheels Car of the Year award.

Throughout the 1980s, the Charade became one of Australia's most popular first cars. In 1988, Daihatsu brought the hot-hatch world the Charade GTti, boasting a 1.0L twin-cam intercooled turbo 3-cylinder (CB70/CB80) producing 74kW and revving to 9,000 rpm. The Handivan and Mira delivery vans also carved out a major niche in Australian metropolitan courier fleets.

In the off-road arena, Daihatsu earned immense respect with the Rocky (F70/F75/F80) and Feroza (F300), offering genuine dual-range four-wheel drive and tough ladder-chassis engineering in a compact footprint. In 2000, Toyota acquired a controlling interest in Daihatsu. Facing tightening margins in the light car segment and Toyota's decision to streamline its small-car strategy around the Echo and Yaris, Daihatsu officially withdrew from the Australian new car market in March 2006.

models_catalog.overview: Australia's favourite 3-cylinder city runabout, Wheels COTY 1979 winner, and GTti pocket rocket.

1.0L petrol and 1.0L CL diesel; first Charade Turbo model introduced in 1984.

models_catalog.name: Feroza
models_catalog.overview: Rugged, removable-hardtop mini 4x4 with independent front suspension and dual-range 4WD.

generations.summary: 1.6L HD-C (carb) then HD-E (EFI) petrol, dual-range transfer case, torsion-bar front and leaf rear.

models_catalog.name: Rocky
models_catalog.overview: Heavy-duty diesel compact 4WD with solid beam axles front and rear, celebrated for tractor-like outback resilience.

generations.summary: 2.8L DL naturally aspirated and DL-T turbo-diesel engines; beam axles and leaf springs.

models_catalog.name: Copen
models_catalog.overview: Charming two-seat roadster featuring an electric retractable aluminum hardtop.

generations.summary: 659cc JB-DET 4-cylinder turbo in initial batch, followed by 1.3L K3-VE 4-cylinder engine.
